_: The King's decrees as data (consolidation B5): what each costs (in hundreds of crowns), its name, and what it does in a few words for the town card (effect; courtEffect when ordered at his own seat). crown.js decides what happens; the view shows these words, never its own. courtOnly: given only as an answer to a matter at court (cmd.matter), never from a town card. oncePerHouse: a house has it of the King once a reign. promise: the free answer to a crisis the purse can't pay (gameplay review #1): the house gains favour, the King's most favoured house (rival) loses it. cede: the free answer to a march on Kingsmere: a royal town for their claim (their host goes home). off: cut from the King's orders (gameplay review cut list: gift crowns did less than a feast for more; sellswords did the levy's job; back and settle were two more peace verbs); the bridge refuses them and the view hides them. peace: 'Make them stop', the one peace verb: the price rises by how cold the two houses are (each point under coldBelow adds 1/coldBelow of the price, up to coldMost times it). march: the King's own host marches and lays siege on arrival (no new men are raised; cost is its provisions); favour, others: what the house and every other great house think of it, when it is ordered. ward: favour is what the house thinks of its heir taken; seasons, how long it cannot rise (gameplay review #2: 20 crowns-hundreds and -5 made it a repeatable free win).
